To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel bimetallic alloy nanocluster with an ultrasmall core and an ultrathin ligand shell is synthesized by precise control of the ratio of the two metal precursors and the reaction time.
a novel Ag-Cu nanocluster has been synthesized, and the crystal structure reveals that a M42(t-BuS)20(t-BuSO3)12 ligand shell has been observed for the first time.
a novel bimetallic alloy Ag-Cu nanocluster with a Cu10Ag 2S7 core has been synthesized by a thiolate-based synthetic route.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of a novel ultrasmall bimetallic Ag-Cu nanocluster, which has been characterized by a combination of techniques including X-ray crystallography, UV-Vis, IR, and NMR spectroscopy, and mass spectrometry.
a new strategy to prepare ultrasmall nanomaterials with a precise composition.
a new type of thiolate ligand and the first Ag-Cu bimetalsulfide nanocluster.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ag-Cu alloy cluster has the highest Ag content in the Ag-Cu bismetallic NCs reported to date.
the sulfonate ligands are introduced into an ultrasmal nanocluster via oxidation of thiolates.
the sulfonate, sulfides and thiolates ligands have been introduced into an ultrasmallest nanocluster.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thiolate ligand can be oxidized to the sulfonate ligands in the presence of Ag+ ions, and the sulfonate can be used as a ligand to stabilize the nanocluster.
the sulfonate ligands are not only used to protect the NCs from aggregation but also play an important role in stabilizing the bare sulfur atoms in the cluster core.
the ligand exchange strategy can be used to construct the ultrasmall bimetallic alloy nanocluster.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sulfonate ligands can be introduced into the NCs by in situ oxidation of the thiolate ligand.
the introduction of sulfonate ligands and S atoms into the cluster can significantly increase the stability of the NCs.
sulfonate ligands can be used to synthesize NCs with a high yield.
